Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finova discovery - decision criteria & next steps

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: low-latency document summarization and search for customer support workflows (peak concurrent sessions ~50).
- Key non-functional reqs: latency targets (p90 token latency ideally < 200ms for short prompts), cost sensitivity for high-volume summarization, and a need for SOC2 + audit log evidence.
- Deployment preference: Closed VPC or dedicated pool; open to hosted API for initial pilot if we can hit latency targets.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Stakeholder map: could you confirm who the economic buyer, security lead, and procurement contact will be? We want to align pricing and SLA expectations to the right people.
2) Decision criteria clarification: we discussed latency and cost trade-offs — can you quantify acceptable ranges (e.g., p90 latency and target cost per 1k requests)?
3) Security artifacts: attaching the draft SLA we discussed and a sample SOC2 summary for your security team to review.

Attached: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (sample SLA)

I'll follow up with a short one-pager on deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for your infra and security teams.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Finova discovery - decision criteria & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary and appreciated the SLA draft. Quick answers from our side: 

Stakeholder map (initial):
- Economic buyer: Rajiv Menon (Head of Product) — will own commercial / budget decisions.
- Technical lead / evaluation: Laura Jensen (You have me for dev/product signoff).
- Security lead: Priya Natarajan (cc'd on procurement thread but out of office this week).
- Procurement: procurement@finova.com (handles contracting / PO).

Decision criteria (priority order):
1) Reliability & SLA (uptime and error handling) — must have audit logs and data isolation controls.
2) Latency for end-user flows — aiming for p90 < 250ms for 1–2k token prompts in production.
3) Cost — target to be below $X per 1k summarization calls in steady state (we'll provide a ballpark in a follow-up).
4) Deployment mode flexibility — prefer dedicated pool or VPC for production; pilot can be on hosted if latency is demonstrably met.

Procurement timeline: aiming to complete vendor evaluation and legal by end of June if pilot results are satisfactory.
I'll loop Priya and procurement once we have the technical attachments and quant targets.

Best,
Laura Jensen
Senior Product Manager, Finova
laura.jensen@finova.com

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova discovery - decision criteria & stakeholder map (post-call)

Thanks Laura — great, that helps a lot. A few clarifying items before we loop security/procurement: 

1) Latency target: you mentioned p90 < 250ms for 1–2k token prompts. For us to size a pilot and recommend a deployment mode, would you accept a staged target:
   - Pilot: p90 < 300ms (hosted with burst/dedicated variant)
   - Production: p90 < 250ms on dedicated or private deployment
\2) Cost sensitivity: can you share a rough target number (even a range) for cost per 1k summarization calls so we can model throughput and batching trade-offs? If you'd rather share offline with procurement, that's fine.
\3) Security artifacts: we'll send the SOC2 summary and an evidence checklist. Neha — can you add the typical audit artifacts and expected delivery times for a demo?
\We will also attach a short matrix comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private (latency, cost, isolation).
\Thanks — cc'ing Rishi and Neha to help with technical + commercial follow-up.
\Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria & stakeholder map (technical clarifications)

Hi Laura — quick technical clar to help with your p90 goal. From our side, typical considerations: 

- Pilot vs production: hosted API can meet p90 ~200–350ms for short prompts (under 512 tokens) depending on region and load. Dedicated pools / private deployments are more predictable and can push p90 < 200ms with optimized batching and KV-cache warmup.
- Prompt length sensitivity: p90 increases with longer prompts / context windows. If your summaries are driven by 1–2k tokens of context, expect higher tail latency; we recommend truncation or pre-filtering for pilot tests.
- Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, and lower-precision quantized models reduce cost but may affect quality. We can run an eval on a subset of your prompts to quantify quality vs quantization.
\Ask for Finova: can you share a representative sample of 50–100 prompts (anonymized) and an expected peak concurrent sessions estimate for pilot (50 was mentioned)? We'll use that to model both latency and cost and provide a recommended deployment (hosted pilot + dedicated production or private if you prefer).
\Attached: finova-security-questionnaire-completed.xlsx (filled with our answers)
\Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
